audit_declarations.declaration:
theorem CantorCharacterization.exists_clopen_split.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [PerfectSpace X]
  (hB : CantorCharacterization.HasClopenBasis X) {U : Set X} (hU : IsClopen U) (hne : Set.Nonempty U) :
  Exists fun V =>
    Exists fun W =>
      And (IsClopen V)
        (And (IsClopen W) (And (Set.Nonempty V) (And (Set.Nonempty W) (And (Disjoint V W) (Eq (Union.union V W) U)))))

audit_declarations.declaration:
theorem CantorCharacterization.exists_deciding_split.{u_1} {X : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [PerfectSpace X]
  (hB : CantorCharacterization.HasClopenBasis X) {U C : Set X} (hU : IsClopen U) (hne : Set.Nonempty U)
  (hC : IsClopen C) :
  Exists fun V =>
    And (Eq (Union.union (V Bool.false) (V Bool.true)) U)
      (And (Disjoint (V Bool.false) (V Bool.true))
        (∀ (b : Bool),
          And (IsClopen (V b)) (And (Set.Nonempty (V b)) (Or (LE.le (V b) C) (LE.le (V b) (Compl.compl C))))))

# Brouwer characterization of Cantor space

Classical source: Anush Tserunyan, Introduction to descriptive set theory,
Theorem 5.3. The proof here uses a binary clopen scheme that decides an
enumerated basis, rather than prescribing diameter reduction at each split.
